contracts.title: CSM14-01 · 18 Jun 2028 — Model branch-safe comparison refresh invariants (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Add immutable Java input/result types and an executable invariant validator for refreshing an owned comparison checkpoint. A checkpoint pins 1–3 unique health product/source-version references, their source digests, scenario, stable slot IDs, display order and a checkpoint revision. A local branch carries its base revision and proposed selection; the Catalog public port supplies an upstream candidate. Model RESOLVED, CONFLICT and UNAVAILABLE as different outcomes. Implement the validator and its tests, not a complete merge algorithm.
contracts.fixture: SYNTHETIC owner A has existing owned shortlist S-A and journey J-A. Checkpoint C-A/r1 has slots s1→H1/v1, s2→H2/v1, s3→H3/v1 in that order, all scenario-health-001; B owns S-B/J-B. Catalog generation 20 includes H1/v2, H2/v1 and H3/v1. All source text is public synthetic wording; no consumer answers or free-text notes are present. An unavailable H3 lookup has status UNAVAILABLE, not an absent selected slot.
acceptance: The validator accepts the valid three-slot fixture and retains the exact base revision/source digests without mutating caller collections.
Repeated product identity, four slots, incompatible scenario or missing source identity produces a typed invalid result with no partial checkpoint.
A source read that is unavailable cannot be represented as an intentional deletion or an unchanged/Included result.
A mutated input list cannot change an already-constructed immutable checkpoint; supply and run that adversarial test.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Record a maximum six-node ownership/data diagram and an executable invariant table. Explain why stable slot identity, source version and checkpoint revision are separate identities. State the maximum 3-slot assumption and a condition that would invalidate the chosen representation.
contracts.novelty: The original curriculum already saves selections/resumes journeys. This new contract starts a distinct branch-versus-upstream refresh model; it does not rebuild save/resume or repeat the final filter/cursor exercise.

contracts.title: CSM14-02 · 19 Jun 2028 — Implement deterministic three-way version reconciliation (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Implement a pure Java three-way reconciliation seam over base B, local branch L and upstream candidate U. For each stable slot, L=B permits U; U=B permits L; L=U permits that shared result; divergent L and U require an explicit conflict. Intentional removal is a typed local operation. Source UNAVAILABLE stays a separate blocking state. Preserve declared slot order and validate the final 1–3 unique same-scenario products. Do not fetch data, persist or resolve conflicts on the learner’s behalf.
contracts.fixture: For s1: B=H1/v1, L=H1/v1, U=H1/v2 gives an unambiguous refresh. For s2: B=H2/v1, L=H2/v2, U=H2/v3 gives conflict. For s3: local explicitly removes while U changes H3/v1→H3/v2, giving a remove-versus-change conflict. A separate no-change fixture has L=B=U. UNAVAILABLE is supplied independently of any missing map entry.
acceptance: Unambiguous cases follow the declared truth table and preserve exact source/version references.
Both divergent-version and remove-versus-change cases expose unresolved conflict; no version wins by timestamp or map iteration order.
No-change reconciliation is idempotent and the input objects remain unchanged.
Reversing fixture map insertion order does not change conflict identities or declared result order; unavailable source evidence never becomes deletion.
Execute at least one independently authored counterexample to the proposed equality/identity rule.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Retain the executable truth table, a measured operation count for 1 and 3 slots, and one rejected last-write-wins counterexample. Explain why constant small bounds do not eliminate semantic conflict and identify which part could generalize to O(n).
contracts.novelty: This implements three-way selection semantics, rather than the old two-version clause diff, stable cursor or latest-per-family query.

contracts.title: CSM14-03 · 20 Jun 2028 — Persist immutable checkpoint revisions atomically (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Implement the prepared Shortlist persistence adapter for appending an immutable checkpoint revision and advancing its head using the existing unit-of-work/public module contracts. Store only owner-scoped references and permitted metadata, not copied private answers. The domain revision, required safe audit and existing relevant journey projection/step change must commit together. Reuse the existing encryption adapter wherever the established data policy requires it; do not create keys or a new payload system.
contracts.fixture: Prepared PostgreSQL schema has C-A/r1 and matching owned shortlist/journey. Append r2 referencing r1 with unchanged scenario and approved exact version identities. A disposable fault fires after staging the revision but before the required audit/journey writes. A separate read after rollback inspects durable state.
acceptance: A successful append preserves r1 byte-for-byte, persists r2 and advances only the appropriate owned head/projection.
The injected failure leaves no r2, no advanced head and no orphan required audit/journey record.
The adapter reaches other modules only through their public contracts; no cross-module repository shortcut is introduced.
A duplicate immutable revision identity with changed content fails rather than overwriting history.
Record the actual transaction boundary and database assertions; fixture-only in-memory results do not prove SQL durability.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Annotate the actual commit boundary and affected rows for success versus injected rollback. Explain the head-pointer/history trade-off and why an audit row rolled back in that transaction is not durable evidence of failure.
contracts.novelty: This adds a new immutable comparison-checkpoint aggregate using existing transaction foundations, not another generic SQL history mock.

contracts.title: CSM14-04 · 21 Jun 2028 — Fence concurrent branch saves and replay (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Implement the checkpoint-save command’s expected-revision check and reuse the existing durable idempotency envelope. Scope an operation to trusted owner, resource and operation kind; compare the canonical request content. Exercise two prepared PostgreSQL connections with barriers, not sleeps. One branch based on r1 may win; a competing changed branch must receive a conflict and retain its draft for explicit re-preview.
contracts.fixture: Tab T1 and T2 both start at C-A/r1. T1 proposes H1/v2; T2 proposes H2/v2. Both are released at a controlled write barrier. Retry T1 with the same operation key/content after its response is suppressed; then reuse that key with T2 content. A second resource has the same textual key but a distinct authorized operation scope.
acceptance: Exactly one concurrent changed branch advances the head from r1; the loser cannot overwrite the winning revision.
The same accepted key/content returns the stored result even after response loss, without a second revision or durable domain effect.
Changed content under the same scoped operation key conflicts and retains the original stored result.
The losing response provides a safe stale-revision outcome, not an instruction to discard/reapply the draft automatically.
The test records the real two-connection schedule and chosen linearization point; sequential mock calls are labeled insufficient concurrency evidence.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Draw at most eight schedule events and identify the database operation that linearizes acceptance. Compare optimistic expected-revision checks with a long-held application lock using the observed contention, not assumed distributed scale.
contracts.novelty: The race protects a new branch head and immutable revisions; it is distinct from the original payment unknown-outcome and browser query-race exercises.
